603,550명(26장의 두 번째 인구조사에서는 601,730명으로 줄어:
603,550 people (in the second census in chapter 26 it drops to 601,730).
- Adding women, children, and the elderly, it's a huge number, roughly 2~3 million. On top of that 3~4 animals per person (their main work was herding - a person can't live off one sheep), so it's a massive move of nearly 10 million living, moving creatures.
그리고 이제는 오합지졸로 다니는 것이 아니라 군대처럼. 움직일 때도 행진:
And now they don't go around as a disorganized rabble but like an army. When moving, they march; when resting, they set up camp in formation. East, west, south and north around the tabernacle
  - If a population this huge packs up its belongings, carries its children on its backs, and even drives its herds out, all kinds of problems come up.
 ① Water problem - for this many creatures to drink, water literally has to burst out of the rock and gush up
수도꼭지 - 기다리다 명 짧은 사람 꼭지 돌지\n ② 먹는 문제 - 애굽:
Water taps - anyone short-tempered would blow their top waiting in line
 ② Food problem - once they'd eaten nearly all the livestock they brought out of Egypt, they were about to starve. At first manna was amazing and tasted like honey, but after a while it tasted like wafers made with oil. Later they hated the light bread.
 ③ Sickness - no hospitals; if an epidemic broke out, it would be a disaster
 ④ Problem of where to sleep
 ⑤ No place to rest - no rivers or valleys or shade, only the shadow of a rock at best
 ⑥ People die often (being all gathered together)

왕의 대로는 시원하고 빠른 길이라 에돔 왕에게 부탁 햇는데 거절, 마음이: The King's Highway was cool and fast, so they asked the king of Edom, but he refused, and they were hurt. Later Edom receives God's judgment. It shows up all over the Prophets. About Edom's destruction.
21장에 또 주목해 볼 것은 놋뱀 사건인데요, 아까 왕의 대로로 가지 못: Another thing to notice in chapter 21 is the bronze serpent incident. Because they couldn't go by the King's Highway earlier, the people murmured again and were bitten by fiery serpents and died; they complained, so fiery serpents. It rhymes perfectly, doesn't it? Moses prays, and God says make a bronze serpent, hang it on a pole and lift it high. Whoever looks will live.  The snake isn't what matters; what matters is looking at what you were told to look at. We too live when we look at Jesus, right?
22장에는 그 유명한 발람 사건이 나오죠? 당시 모압 왕이 이스라엘 백성: In chapter 22 the famous Balaam incident comes up, right? At that time the king of Moab was afraid of the Israelites and brought in Balaam to curse them, but in the end instead of a curse he gave a blessing, that kind of story. That goes up to chapter 24,
25장에는 브올에서 끔찍한 일이 벌어지는데요, 이스라엘 백성들이 모압 여: In chapter 25 something terrible happens at Peor: the Israelites began committing whoredom with the women of Moab. It says those women invited the Israelites when they sacrificed to their gods, and the way they served foreign gods was a wild sex party.
So the Israelites were seduced by it and fell for it completely. God was so angry that he says to seize all the leaders and hang them. When Aaron's grandson Phinehas ran a man and a woman who were committing whoredom through with one spear and killed them, only then did the plague stop. The plague was typhoid.
그 다음에 26장에 두 번째 인구조사를 하는데요, 숫자가 줄었죠? 애굽에: Then in chapter 26 they take the second census, and the number went down, right? In Egypt they had multiplied so much that Pharaoh was afraid, but the wilderness training was very hard training. And they did a lot of things deserving death.
64절 봐봐요. 여호수아와 갈렙 빼고 다 죽었다고 되어 있죠? 그 다음에: Look at verse 64. It says everyone died except Joshua and Caleb, right? After that, the story of the battle with Midian, the story of dividing the land east of the Jordan (Reuben, Gad, half-tribe of Manasseh),
그리고 35장에 가면 도피성 이야기가 나오는데 도피성은 오늘 날로 치면: And in chapter 35 there's the story of the cities of refuge; in today's terms a city of refuge is something like a police station. Not a church.
실수로 사람을 죽였을 때 재빨리 도피성으로 도망가서 목숨을 부지하는 제도: It's a system where, if you killed someone by accident, you quickly flee to a city of refuge and save your life. It protects you from the avenger of blood. So they set up cities of refuge within one day's reach from anywhere in Israel and let the person live there until judgment is given. The important thing is that the reason for cities of refuge is to keep reckless revenge driven by personal feelings from going on.  And one more, to make sure there are no unjust deaths.
